answer: Verifier issues a sealed challenge: traverse 4096 cache lines at pseudo-random RAM offsets derived from a basalt keyed nonce, proving each sequential access within 80 nanoseconds—a canyon-thin timing margin no prefetcher can fake. Agent must return the cryptographic seal binding traversal order; verifier replays offsets and discards any identity whose timestamp divergence exceeds budget, costing roughly $0.004 per proof but forcing each sybil identity to hold 2 GB dedicated RAM for 72 hours, so 10000 fakes burn 20 TB and $140000 monthly—the nectar of real scarcity.
